niche.habitat: Cliff bases, lava tube entrances, leeward slopes, and hidden cave perimeters.
niche.diet: Carnivore/Omnivore: flesh, insects, carrion, and alkaloid plants for self-medication.
niche.active: Nocturnal and crepuscular; avoids midday heat and dense fog.

body: Belly-low prowler with silent, padded feet that dampen sound in the dense atmosphere and a flexible spine that allows it to freeze in lulls and move synchronously with the wind gusts. Its leeward ambush strategy exploits the 1.6× drag and fog to mask its approach.

links: It keeps its belly at grass height, where eyes lose it
Dawn fog blinds prey most mornings, so hiding low always works
Gales shove with 1.6x Earth's force, so only low builds stayed to hunt

skill.effect: When lying flat, the creature blends into the terrain and moves with deliberate slowness, making it nearly impossible to spot from a distance.

chains.weakness: Flattened grass marks its bed; beat the bush and it bolts.

journal.en: It hunts at the height of the grass.

plausibility.summary: Frame gales (F19) as favouring a low centre of mass and crouched stalk on exposed meadow edges, not as eliminating taller predators island-wide; tall fast hunters (e.g. Garfio-type lineages) persist in other niches.
fixes: Frame gales (F19) as favouring a low centre of mass and crouched stalk on exposed meadow edges, not as eliminating taller predators island-wide; tall fast hunters (e.g. Garfio-type lineages) persist in other niches.

analogues.organism: Felids (e.g. serval, leopard): ventral-flexed stalk in grass; body held below herbivore eye height — classic ambush crypsis.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Dense air carries every footfall to prey's ears
Soft pads and placed steps kill the thump
Silence costs speed, so it walks and saves the burst

skill.effect: It moves completely silently when walking, but its heavy footsteps echo loudly whenever it breaks into a run.

chains.weakness: Listen for the burst; it cannot chase quietly.

journal.en: You hear it only when it decides to run.

analogues.organism: Felidae: soft digital and metacarpal pads damp impact sounds during slow stalk; trade-off between silent walk and audible sprint (same family, multiple species).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Westerlies drag scent east across the meadows
It beds on the lee side, its smell blowing away from prey
Thick air punishes a missed pounce, so it strikes once, from close

skill.effect: When it ambushes from the shadows, the creature launches a powerful strike that catches its target completely off guard, though it must rest briefly before attempting another.

chains.weakness: Circle upwind: it scents you at 30 m and aborts.

journal.en: It lets the wind carry the mistake away.

analogues.organism: Grey wolf (Canis lupus) and African lion (Panthera leo): approach from downwind so prey scent-receptors are not alerted; single close-range spring on ambush cats.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Freezes in lulls, moves with gusts
links: Gale wind roars and grass whips, drowning eyes and ears
A low, heavy build leans into wind that staggers taller hunters
It moves with the gusts and locks still in the lulls

skill.effect: During fierce windstorms, the creature crouches low and becomes nearly invisible, firmly planting its feet so the howling gusts cannot budge it.

chains.weakness: Calm air strips the mask: track it at clear midday, when eyes win.
observe: moves only as gusts shake the grass
leaning into wind that staggers others

journal.en: It moves when the wind does; watch the lulls.

plausibility.summary: Treat as a seasonal/windy-weather tactic (winter gales, F19), not default midday behaviour; require enough body mass and low profile so gust knockback immunity is biomechanical, not magical.
fixes: Treat as a seasonal/windy-weather tactic (winter gales, F19), not default midday behaviour; require enough body mass and low profile so gust knockback immunity is biomechanical, not magical.

analogues.organism: Disturbance masking in sensory ecology — animals time movement or calls to periodic environmental noise (e.g. wind, streams); from memory, unverified: Brumm & Slabbekoorn ~2005 on noise and acoustic communication. Grass ripple timed movement parallels motion-hiding while vegetation moves.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

temperament: Patient stalker that values silence and wind timing over speed, striking only when the odds are absolute.
moments: Freezing perfectly still as a Zanco herd passes overhead, then surging forward in perfect sync with a sudden evening gust.
A silent pounce from a lava tube overhang that catches a lone Rondo.
Night eyes glowing faintly under the moon as it tracks a carcass drift.
